stories.actor: A man who sold land to Rav Pappa
stories.event: A man sold land to Rav Pappa because he needed money to buy oxen.
stories.turn: In the end he did not need the money.
stories.outcome: Rav Pappa returned the land to him, beyond the letter of the law.
stories.summary: A man sold land to Rav Pappa to raise money for oxen. When it turned out he did not need the money, Rav Pappa gave him back his land, going beyond what the law required.

stories.actor: The people of Neharde'a and Rav Nahman
stories.event: During a drought in Neharde'a everyone sold their mansions to buy wheat.
stories.turn: Wheat then arrived and the sales proved unnecessary.
stories.outcome: Rav Nahman ruled that the mansions return to their owners.
stories.summary: In a drought in Neharde'a, everyone sold their mansions to buy wheat. Then wheat arrived. Rav Nahman ruled that the mansions go back to their original owners.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yehuda, Sumakhos, and Rabbi Yosei
stories.event: After Rabbi Meir's death, Rabbi Yehuda barred Rabbi Meir's students from his study hall, but Sumakhos pushed in and quoted a ruling of Rabbi Meir.
stories.turn: Rabbi Yehuda became angry and dismissed the ruling as irrelevant, since a woman would not be in the Temple courtyard.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yosei spoke up, refusing to stay silent, and showed the ruling was relevant.
stories.summary: After Rabbi Meir died, Rabbi Yehuda told his students not to let Rabbi Meir's quarrelsome students in. Sumakhos forced his way in and cited a ruling from Rabbi Meir about betrothal with a priest's portion. Rabbi Yehuda angrily dismissed it as pointless, but Rabbi Yosei said he would not let the Torah suffer through silence and explained cases where the ruling matters.

stories.actor: A man who sold his property to move to Eretz Yisrael
stories.event: A man sold his property intending to move to Eretz Yisrael.
stories.turn: He went but could not settle there, and sought to cancel the sale.
stories.outcome: Rava ruled the sale could be nullified (another version: that it could not).
stories.summary: A man sold his property in order to move to Eretz Yisrael. He went but was unable to settle, and on returning wanted to undo the sale. Rava ruled that since he went intending to settle and failed, he could cancel it; another version reports the opposite ruling.

stories.actor: Another man who sold his property to move to Eretz Yisrael
stories.event: A man sold his property intending to move to Eretz Yisrael.
stories.turn: In the end he did not go.
stories.outcome: Rav Ashi ruled that he could have gone had he wished, so the sale stands.
stories.summary: Another man sold his property to move to Eretz Yisrael but never went. Rav Ashi ruled that going was in his own hands, so he could not cancel the sale.

stories.actor: A daughter left a palm tree in her father's will
stories.event: A man willed a palm tree to his daughter.
stories.turn: The heirs divided the estate and gave her no tree at all.
stories.outcome: Abaye ruled they must give her a tree and redivide the estate.
stories.summary: A man left instructions that his daughter receive a palm tree. The heirs divided the property and gave her nothing, each implying it was in another's share. Rav Yosef compared it to the mishna, but Abaye ruled the heirs must give her a tree and divide the estate afresh.

stories.actor: A second daughter left a palm tree
stories.event: A man willed a palm tree to his daughter but died leaving only two half-shares of palm trees.
stories.turn: The heirs wanted to give her the two halves, and Rav Ashi questioned whether that counts as a palm tree.
stories.outcome: Rav Mordekhai reported Rava's view that two halves count as a palm tree.
stories.summary: A man left his daughter a palm tree but owned only halves of two trees. The heirs offered her the two halves. Rav Ashi was unsure if that fulfilled the will, and Rav Mordekhai told him, in Rava's name, that people do call two halves a palm tree.

stories.actor: Rav Hiyya bar Adda and Reish Lakish
stories.event: Rav Hiyya bar Adda, a schoolteacher, was absent three days harvesting a vine his father left him.
stories.turn: The vine's yield dropped each day.
stories.outcome: Reish Lakish told him the yield would have been greater had he not neglected the children's Torah study.
stories.summary: Rav Hiyya bar Adda, who taught children for Reish Lakish, missed three days of teaching. He explained he was harvesting an enormously fruitful vine, though its yield fell each day. Reish Lakish told him the vine would have produced even more had he not left his teaching.

stories.actor: Rami bar Yehezkel
stories.event: Rami bar Yehezkel came to Benei Berak and saw goats grazing under fig trees.
stories.turn: Honey dripped from the figs and milk from the goats, mixing together.
stories.outcome: He declared this is what 'flowing with milk and honey' means.
stories.summary: Visiting Benei Berak, Rami bar Yehezkel saw goats under fig trees, with honey dripping from the figs and milk from the goats mingling on the ground. He said this was the meaning of a land flowing with milk and honey.

stories.actor: Rabbi Helbo, Rabbi Avira and Rabbi Yosei bar Hanina
stories.event: Three Sages visiting a place were served a peach as large as a five-se'a stewpot.
stories.turn: The peach was too big to finish.
stories.outcome: They ate a third, declared a third ownerless, and gave a third to their animals.
stories.summary: Three Sages came to a certain place and were served a peach the size of a large stewpot. They ate one third, left one third ownerless, and fed the last third to their animals.

stories.actor: The daughter-in-law of Nakdimon ben Guryon
stories.event: The Sages allotted her two se'a of wine a week for pudding from her husband's estate.
stories.turn: She blessed them that they should allot the same to their own daughters.
stories.outcome: Since she was a widow awaiting levirate marriage, they did not answer amen.
stories.summary: After her husband died, the Sages allotted Nakdimon ben Guryon's daughter-in-law a large weekly portion of wine. She blessed them that their daughters should receive the same. Because she was a widow awaiting her yavam, they did not answer amen.

stories.actor: Homa, Abaye's widow, Rava, and Rava's wife
stories.event: Homa asked Rava for sustenance and wine; while showing the size of Abaye's cups her arm was exposed.
stories.turn: Her beauty lit up the court, and Rava went home aroused; his wife learned who had been there.
stories.outcome: Rava's wife beat Homa with a chest lock and drove her out of Mehoza.
stories.summary: Abaye's widow Homa came to Rava for support and asked for wine, claiming Abaye gave her large cups of it. As she gestured, her arm was uncovered and her beauty lit the courtroom. Rava went home and approached his wife, who discovered why, chased Homa out of town beating her, and accused her of having killed three husbands and coming for a fourth.

stories.actor: The wife of Rav Yosef son of Rava
stories.event: She asked Rav Nehemya for sustenance and wine.
stories.turn: He considered whether she was entitled to wine.
stories.outcome: He granted it because the people of Mehoza drink wine.
stories.summary: The widow of Rav Yosef son of Rava asked Rav Nehemya to set her sustenance and wine. He granted both, explaining that the people of Mehoza customarily drink wine.

stories.actor: The wife of Rav Yosef son of Rav Menashya of D'vil
stories.event: She asked Rav Yosef for sustenance, wine, and silk garments.
stories.turn: He asked why she needed silk.
stories.outcome: She answered: for you, your friends, and your friends' friends.
stories.summary: A widow came before Rav Yosef and asked for sustenance and wine, which he granted. When she also asked for silk and he asked why, she replied that it was so she would not be shamed before him and his colleagues.

stories.actor: A man who betrothed a girl with vegetables
stories.event: A man betrothed a minor girl, without her father's consent, with a bundle of vegetables in the marketplace.
stories.turn: The question arose whether the father might have approved.
stories.outcome: Ravina ruled there was no concern because the betrothal was degrading.
stories.summary: A man betrothed a minor girl in the marketplace with a bundle of vegetables. Ravina ruled that because this was a degrading way to betroth, there was no concern that the father had approved. Asked which part was degrading, he said both.

stories.actor: A father, mother, and the father's relative
stories.event: Parents disputed which relative their daughter should marry, and the father gave in to the mother.
stories.turn: During the betrothal meal, the father's relative climbed to the roof and betrothed her himself.
stories.outcome: The Sages ruled the father did not want that betrothal.
stories.summary: A father wanted his daughter to marry his relative, the mother wanted hers, and he finally gave in. While everyone ate at the betrothal feast, the father's relative went up to the roof and betrothed the girl. Abaye and Rava gave reasons why the father is presumed not to have wanted this.

stories.actor: The Elders of Nezonya, Rav Hamnuna and Rav Hisda
stories.event: The Elders of Nezonya skipped Rav Hisda's lecture, and he sent Rav Hamnuna to ostracize them.
stories.turn: They posed Rav Hamnuna a question he could not answer and mocked his name.
stories.outcome: Rav Hamnuna returned to Rav Hisda, who showed him the answer was in a baraita.
stories.summary: When the Elders of Nezonya stayed away from his lecture, Rav Hisda sent Rav Hamnuna to ostracize them. They said Rav Hisda had not answered their question, and when Rav Hamnuna invited them to ask him instead, he could not answer either, so they mocked him as 'Karnuna'. He went back to Rav Hisda, who told him the answer was in a known baraita.

stories.actor: Rav Amram the Pious
stories.event: Redeemed captive women were lodged in Rav Amram's attic, and seeing one's beauty he lifted a huge ladder and began to climb.
stories.turn: Halfway up he stopped himself and shouted 'Fire in Amram's house!'
stories.outcome: He drove out his evil inclination, which left him like a pillar of fire, and told it he was superior to it.
stories.summary: Captive women were brought to Rav Amram's house and the ladder was removed. Seeing one of them, he lifted a ladder ten men could not lift and started up. Halfway, he braced himself and cried 'fire', summoning the Sages; when they said he had shamed them, he said better shame now than in the World-to-Come, and he expelled his evil inclination as a pillar of fire.

stories.actor: Rabbi Meir
stories.event: Rabbi Meir mocked sinners, and Satan appeared to him as a woman across a river.
stories.turn: He began crossing a rope bridge after her.
stories.outcome: Halfway across Satan left him, saying only heaven's warning about him had saved him.
stories.summary: Rabbi Meir used to scoff at sinners. Satan appeared as a woman on the far bank, and Rabbi Meir started across a rope bridge toward her. Halfway, Satan let go and said that only the heavenly proclamation protecting him had kept him from ruin.

stories.actor: Rabbi Akiva
stories.event: Rabbi Akiva mocked sinners, and Satan appeared to him as a woman atop a palm tree.
stories.turn: He began climbing the tree.
stories.outcome: Halfway up Satan left him, saying only heaven's warning about him had saved him.
stories.summary: Rabbi Akiva also scoffed at sinners. Satan appeared as a woman at the top of a palm tree and Rabbi Akiva began to climb. Halfway up Satan let go, saying only the heavenly proclamation had saved him.

stories.actor: Peleimu
stories.event: Peleimu daily taunted Satan, who came to him on Yom Kippur eve as a repulsive pauper and was seated at his table.
stories.turn: The pauper spat in a cup, was rebuked, and pretended to die, so people said Peleimu killed a man.
stories.outcome: Satan revealed himself to the hiding Peleimu and told him to say 'May the Merciful One rebuke Satan' instead.
stories.summary: Peleimu used to say 'an arrow in Satan's eye' every day. On Yom Kippur eve Satan came as a sore-covered beggar, demanded to eat inside at the table, behaved disgustingly, then collapsed as if dead, and people cried that Peleimu had killed him. Peleimu hid in the outhouse; Satan followed, revealed himself, and told him to change his taunt to a prayer that God rebuke Satan.

stories.actor: Rabbi Hiyya bar Ashi and his wife
stories.event: Rabbi Hiyya bar Ashi always prayed to be saved from the evil inclination.
stories.turn: His wife overheard and wondered why, since he had abstained from her for years.
stories.outcome: The window ends before the outcome.
stories.summary: Rabbi Hiyya bar Ashi prayed daily to be saved from the evil inclination. His wife heard him and wondered why, since he had withdrawn from her for years because of his age. The story continues past the window.

stories.actor: Rabbi Shimon bar Abba, Rabbi Elai and Rabbi Ya'akov bar Zavdi
stories.event: Two rabbis studying Torah stood up when Rabbi Shimon bar Abba passed.
stories.turn: He objected that they were ordained and he was not, and that Torah need not stand for its students.
stories.outcome: He told them they need not have stood.
stories.summary: Rabbi Elai and Rabbi Ya'akov bar Zavdi were studying when Rabbi Shimon bar Abba walked by, and they rose for him. He told them they need not have, since they were ordained and he was only an associate, and since those studying Torah need not rise for its scholars.

stories.actor: Rav Ika bar Avin, Abaye and Rav Hananel
stories.event: Rav Ika bar Avin reported in Rav's name that Hillazon Nihavnad has unflawed lineage.
stories.turn: Abaye accused him of bias, since a yevama from there had fallen to him.
stories.outcome: They asked Rav Hananel, who confirmed the ruling was Rav's.
stories.summary: Rav Ika bar Avin taught that Hillazon Nihavnad has unflawed lineage. Abaye told people to ignore him, since he had a personal interest in a widow from there. Rav Ika said the ruling came from Rav Hananel, and when they asked, Rav Hananel confirmed it.

stories.actor: Rav Ashi, Mar Zutra and the king's butler
stories.event: Seeing Mar Zutra grow pale with craving as the king's food passed, Rav Ashi put some in his mouth.
stories.turn: The butler said he spoiled the king's meal; Rav Ashi said the meat was diseased and pointed to the exact spot.
stories.outcome: They found the leprous defect, and Rav Ashi explained he had seen a leprous spirit over it.
stories.summary: Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi sat at King Izgur's gate as his butler carried food by. Rav Ashi saw Mar Zutra blanch with craving and put some food in his mouth. Accused of ruining the king's meal, he claimed the meat was leprous; when nothing was found, he pointed to a spot where it was found, explaining he had seen a leprous spirit hovering over it.

stories.actor: A Roman and a woman
stories.event: A Roman proposed to a woman who refused, so he ate pomegranates before her without sharing until she became ill.
stories.turn: He offered to cure her if she would marry him, and she agreed.
stories.outcome: He had her spit out her saliva while he ate pomegranates, a green leaf-like thing came out, and she was cured.
stories.summary: A Roman asked a woman to marry him and she said no. He ate pomegranates in front of her, giving her none, until swallowing her craving made her ill. He then offered to cure her if she married him; she agreed, and by spitting out her saliva as he ate she expelled something like a green leaf and recovered.

stories.actor: Rabbi Akiva, his wife, and ben Kalba Savua
stories.event: Ben Kalba Savua's daughter betrothed herself to his shepherd Akiva on condition he study, and her father disinherited her.
stories.turn: Akiva studied 24 years and returned with 24,000 students; his wife was recognized, and her father came seeking release from his vow.
stories.outcome: Akiva revealed who he was, and ben Kalba Savua bowed to him and gave him half his wealth.
stories.summary: Rabbi Akiva was ben Kalba Savua's shepherd; the rich man's daughter secretly married him on condition he go study, and her father threw her out and vowed she would get nothing. Akiva studied twelve years, overheard her urging him to stay longer, and studied twelve more, returning with 24,000 students; he honored her before them, saying all their Torah was hers. Her father came to have his vow annulled, said he would never have vowed had he known Akiva would learn even a little, and when Akiva revealed himself he fell at his feet and gave him half his fortune.

stories.actor: Rav Yosef son of Rava and his father
stories.event: Rav Yosef son of Rava, sent to study for six years, left after three to visit his wife on Yom Kippur eve.
stories.turn: His father came out to meet him with a weapon and rebuked him.
stories.outcome: Both were so caught up in the argument that neither ate the pre-fast meal.
stories.summary: Rava sent his son to study with Rav Yosef for six years. After three, on the eve of Yom Kippur, the son set out to visit his wife. Rava met him armed and rebuked him for remembering his wife, and in the quarrel neither ate the meal before the fast.

stories.actor: Disputing heirs and Rav Nahman
stories.event: A Sage threatened heirs with excommunication unless they appeased the others and sent them to Rav Nahman.
stories.turn: Rav Nahman considered the change in the estate's value.
stories.outcome: He ruled the heirs acquired rights according to the estate's value at the father's death.
stories.summary: Picking up mid-story, a Sage warned some heirs he would excommunicate them if they did not appease the others, then sent them to Rav Nahman. Rav Nahman ruled that, just as with depreciated property, when property appreciated the heirs' rights are fixed at the time of the father's death.

stories.actor: A purchaser of two mansions and a creditor
stories.event: A debtor sold two mansions; his creditor seized one and then sought the other.
stories.turn: The purchaser offered: accept the first as full payment, or take 1,000 dinars and leave both.
stories.outcome: Rava ruled the creditor must accept, since he loses nothing.
stories.summary: A man owing 1,000 dinars sold his two mansions for 500 each. The creditor seized one, then came for the other. The buyer offered him either to accept the first as full payment or take 1,000 dinars and release both; Rami bar Hama compared it to the mishna, but Rava ruled the creditor loses nothing and should accept.

stories.actor: A purchaser of two plots and a creditor
stories.event: A debtor sold two plots; his creditor seized one and then sought the other.
stories.turn: The purchaser offered: accept the first as full payment, or take 100 dinars and leave both.
stories.outcome: Abaye ruled the creditor must accept, since he loses nothing.
stories.summary: A man owing 100 dinars sold two small plots for 50 each. The creditor seized one and came for the other. The buyer offered the same choice; Rav Yosef compared it to the mishna, but Abaye ruled the creditor loses nothing and should accept.

stories.actor: Two men drinking wine in Babylonia
stories.event: One man gave the other a cup of wine as betrothal of the other's daughter to his son.
stories.turn: The question arose whether the son had consented.
stories.outcome: Ravina ruled no betrothal: we do not assume the son agreed.
stories.summary: Two men were drinking under poplar trees in Babylonia, and one handed the other a cup of wine to betroth the other's daughter to his son. Ravina ruled that we do not assume the son approved, and he rejected the Sages' suggestions that the son had appointed his father or made his wishes known.

stories.actor: A man who betrothed a girl with vegetables
stories.event: A man betrothed a minor girl with a bundle of vegetables in the marketplace.
stories.turn: The question arose whether the father might have approved.
stories.outcome: Ravina ruled there was no concern because the betrothal was degrading.
stories.summary: A man betrothed a minor girl in the marketplace with a bundle of vegetables. Ravina ruled that because this was degrading, there was no concern that the father had approved, and said both the vegetables and the marketplace made it degrading.

stories.actor: A father, mother, and the father's relative
stories.event: Parents disputed which relative their daughter should marry, and the father gave in to the mother.
stories.turn: During the betrothal meal, the father's relative climbed to the roof and betrothed her himself.
stories.outcome: The Sages ruled the father did not want that betrothal.
stories.summary: A father wanted his daughter to marry his relative, the mother wanted hers, and he finally gave in. During the feast the father's relative went up to the roof and betrothed her. Abaye and Rava gave reasons why the father is presumed not to have wanted it.

stories.actor: A groom, his bride, and Rabban Gamliel bar Rabbi
stories.event: A groom complained he found no blood, while the bride insisted she was a virgin.
stories.turn: Rabban Gamliel had the cloth soaked and laundered and found drops of blood.
stories.outcome: He told the groom to go take possession of his acquisition.
stories.summary: A man came to Rabban Gamliel bar Rabbi saying he found no blood on his wedding night; his bride said she had been a virgin. Rabban Gamliel had the cloth soaked and washed and found drops of blood. He told the groom his bride was a virgin.

stories.actor: A groom, his bride, and Rabban Gamliel bar Rabbi
stories.event: A groom complained he found no blood, while the bride insisted she was still a virgin.
stories.turn: Rabban Gamliel tested two maidservants on a wine barrel, then tested the bride, and no wine scent came from her.
stories.outcome: He told the groom to go take possession of his acquisition.
stories.summary: Another groom said he found no blood and his bride said she was still a virgin. Rabban Gamliel bar Rabbi seated a virgin and a non-virgin maidservant on a wine barrel and found the wine's scent came only from the non-virgin. When the bride was tested, no scent came, and he told the groom she was a virgin.

stories.actor: A woman, her brothers, and Ameimar
stories.event: A woman came before Ameimar claiming a tenth of her father's estate.
stories.turn: Her brothers said they would pay her off in cash if they had the money.
stories.outcome: Ameimar stayed silent, showing he agreed they could pay her in money.
stories.summary: Rav Minyumi was with Ameimar when a woman came claiming a tenth of her father's estate for her dowry. Her brothers told her they would buy her out with money if they had it. Ameimar said nothing, which Rav Minyumi took to mean he accepted that she could be paid off in cash.

stories.actor: Rav Anan, Rav Huna, Rav Sheshet and Mar Ukva
stories.event: Rav Anan wrote to Rav Huna, addressing him as 'our friend', instructing him to give a woman a tenth of the estate.
stories.turn: Rav Huna, offended, sent back a sharp reply via Rav Sheshet: 'Anan, Anan... who sits at the head of the marzeiha?'
stories.outcome: Mar Ukva told Rav Anan he had been wrong to address Rav Huna as a peer when he did not even know what marzeiha meant.
stories.summary: Rav Anan sent Rav Huna a letter calling him 'Huna our friend' and telling him to give a woman her dowry share. Rav Huna made Rav Sheshet, on pain of excommunication, deliver a curt reply mocking Rav Anan. Rav Anan, puzzled and hurt, consulted Mar Ukva, who told him that someone who did not know what marzeiha (mourner) meant had no business calling Rav Huna his friend.

stories.actor: Mar Zutra and a rebellious wife
stories.event: A woman refused her husband, saying he disgusted her.
stories.turn: Mar Zutra compelled her to stay with him.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Hanina of Sura was born of the couple, though the Gemara attributes this to heavenly help.
stories.summary: A woman rebelled against her husband, saying he disgusted her, and Mar Zutra forced her to remain married. From that couple came Rabbi Hanina of Sura. The Gemara says this was heavenly assistance and not a precedent.

stories.actor: Rav Zevid's daughter-in-law and Rav Gamda
stories.event: Rav Zevid's daughter-in-law rebelled while holding a garment, and Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi ruled on her worn clothes.
stories.turn: Rav Gamda accused them of bending the law out of regard for Rav Zevid, since Rava left the question unresolved.
stories.outcome: The ruling became: what she seized is not taken from her; what she did not seize is not given.
stories.summary: Rav Zevid's daughter-in-law rebelled against her husband while holding a garment. Three Sages ruled on whether she lost her worn clothes, and Rav Gamda accused them of flattering (or, in another version, bending the law against) the great Rav Zevid, since Rava had left it open. The outcome: she keeps what she holds and gets nothing more.

stories.actor: Rabbi Tarfon and his mother
stories.event: Rabbi Tarfon bent down so his mother could step on him getting in and out of bed.
stories.turn: He boasted of it in the study hall.
stories.outcome: They told him he had not reached half the honor due her.
stories.summary: Rabbi Tarfon would bend down so his mother could climb onto and off her bed by stepping on him. When he boasted of this in the study hall, the Sages told him he had not reached half of what honoring her requires, asking whether she had ever thrown his purse into the sea without him shaming her.

stories.actor: Rav Asi and his elderly mother
stories.event: Rav Asi's senile mother made escalating demands, including a husband as handsome as him, so he left for Eretz Yisrael.
stories.turn: Hearing she was following him, he got Rabbi Yohanan's blessing to leave the land to meet her.
stories.outcome: On the way he learned her coffin was arriving and said had he known, he would not have left.
stories.summary: Rav Asi's aged mother demanded jewelry and then a husband as handsome as her son, so he left for Eretz Yisrael. When he heard she was following, he asked Rabbi Yohanan about leaving the land to meet her and received an ambiguous blessing, which Rabbi Elazar assured him was permission. Meanwhile he heard that her coffin was on its way and said that had he known, he would not have gone out.
